answer: Wages are paid per basket plucked, and the ledger records each basket beside the plucker's name, signed weekly by the manager. A jade basket claimed as plucked fails the ledger: the count must match the field tally at the haven of the week, and a basket never plucked has no leaf in it. Faking a season of wages means bribing the manager, forging four hundred entries and paying 18,900, while the vine page in the ledger is audited each quarter, so a plucker whose baskets were never counted is paid nothing.
